column1: # npm package versions that a GitHub or OpenSSF malware advisory, or the research post an
# incident links to, names as malware. One line each, tab separated.
#   version   the exact version, or * when every version of that name is malware
# The level: a GitHub or OpenSSF malware advisory decides it, unless the package's own maintainer says
# its malware could not run. A third party's reading (Socket's, Wiz's) is noted, not followed. One
# exception, Injective: its malware advisory, GHSA-5fc4-fm2x-6f4r, says to treat any seed phrase or
# private key used with 1.20.21 as compromised and describes code that sends out only those, with no
# install script, so its level is update, with the advice to move those wallets' funds.
#   Axios, Bitwarden, OpenSearch, tensorlake and Injective: the versions their advisories name. And
#     tensorlake's six native packages (tensorlake-native-*) at 0.5.144: Tensorlake's own GitHub advisory,
#     GHSA-8g63-53c9-65j2, names them as compromised with tensorlake 0.5.144. No malware entry names them,
#     so each has a skip line below for tools/check-advisories.sh.
#   TanStack wave, May 2026: every npm version in the affected-packages list of Wiz's post on it,
#     each also named by a GitHub or OpenSSF malware advisory: the 42 @tanstack packages (a GitHub
#     malware advisory for each, such as GHSA-5v49-5jh3-j7wg, naming the versions TanStack's own
#     advisory, GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx, names) and the packages the worm spread to (tanstack), the
#     OpenSearch client (GHSA-298w-vvm4-ww55, opensearch), and the @mistralai builds (GHSA-3q49-cfcf-g5fm,
#     GHSA-2rm2-c4pc-xxr9, GHSA-rccm-wwph-vgxc) and the @uipath builds (malware advisories such as
#     GHSA-cx9h-9vrc-7393), versions to update because their maintainers say the malware could not
#     run: Mistral (mistral), and UiPath, whose trust center says a bug left it non-functional and the
#     packages pose no risk (uipath). And wot-api 0.8.5, which Wiz's list leaves out: OpenSSF's
#     MAL-2026-3591 adds it to GitHub's 0.8.1 to 0.8.4, and npm's registry shows it published an hour
#     The five versions Wiz's list also names from April's SAP and Intercom compromise are the next
#   Mini Shai-Hulud, April 2026 (minishai), from Wiz's post on it: @cap-js/db-service 2.10.1,
#     @cap-js/postgres 2.2.2 and @cap-js/sqlite 2.2.2 (malware advisories of 29 and 30 April 2026, and
#     cap-js/cds-dbs's GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8), mbt 1.2.48 (OpenSSF's MAL-2026-3179), and intercom-client
#     7.0.4 (Intercom's GHSA-54pg-9963-v8vg and GitHub's GHSA-4594-wxqv-j3pm; Wiz's update says 7.0.5,
#     which no advisory names). Its PyPI release, lightning 2.6.2 and 2.6.3, is in data/bad-pypi.tsv.
#   Mastra, June 2026: the 89 @mastra packages, mastra and create-mastra that GitHub lists, and
#     easy-day-js 1.11.22, which Socket says each of the 141 compromised @mastra packages pulled in.
#     The other 52 of those 141 have no line: Socket says the only change in each was a dependency on
#     easy-day-js ^1.11.21, whose 1.11.22 carried the install hook, so an install of one ran the malware
#     only by pulling in easy-day-js 1.11.22, which its line finds wherever that install is: a
#     lockfile, a global install or npm's cache.
#     And mastraqqq at every version (GHSA-7vj9-63m9-3x7f), a typosquat of mastra that Socket's page on
#     the campaign lists, with caspian-day-js 1.11.23 (OpenSSF's MAL-2026-5892), the dropper its
#   AntV, May 2026 (antv): every version of every OpenSSF malware entry, not withdrawn, that names the
#     takeover of the npm account atool in the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign (OSV's npm export of 25 October
#     2026), 638 versions of 317 packages, less @antv/li-sam-assets 0.1.4, skipped below: 637, as SafeDep
#     counts them. @antv's and others that account published, such as echarts-for-react, size-sensor and
#     timeago.js, the 317 of SafeDep's list of the wave. GitHub's malware advisories name the same
#     versions for 265 (for 120 of them, advisories GitHub imported from those OpenSSF entries on 26 and
#     27 July 2026, such as GHSA-26gq-5v8w-2h84); for 50, OpenSSF's entry adds versions GitHub's leaves out,
#     @antv/a8's spans every version and @antv/li-sam-assets's names only 0.1.4 (below). And the six packages of a
#     second account, jiulingyun, published in the same wave (02:53 to 02:55 UTC on 19 May by npm's
#     registry), each in Wiz's list of the wave, with a GitHub malware advisory of that day (such as
#     GHSA-w2fv-p53h-wcph) and an OpenSSF entry that puts it in the same worm: openclaw-cn 0.3.0,
#     published on 18 May by npm's registry: its OpenSSF entry, MAL-2026-4161, and GitHub's
#     GHSA-qj5h-p6mj-66pf cite only the AntV wave's posts, though SafeDep's list of the wave leaves it out.
#     Nothing else of the wave is named by Wiz's list, by GitHub's malware advisories of 18 to 21 May or
#   Red Hat Cloud Services, June 2026 (redhat): the 32 @redhat-cloud-services packages whose OpenSSF
#     entries name the worm's takeover of the trusted publisher they share, 96 versions. GitHub's malware
#     advisories (such as GHSA-942v-f47r-w9c3) name the same versions for 22, and for 10 OpenSSF's entry
#     adds one or two GitHub's leaves out.
#   keyv, August 2026: keyv 6.0.0, the nine cacheable versions and ecto 5.0.1, which carried the
#     payload, and hamus.js 0.4.1, which OpenSSF's MAL-2026-11974 puts in the same account's compromise
#     (keyv); the 19 @keyv 6.0.0 builds (keyvscope): Socket says they were published without the install
#     hook, but GitHub's malware advisories say a machine that installed one is compromised, and those
#     govern; and the packages the worm spread to (keyvspread), from @thiennq/docs-viewer at 09:38 on 4
#     August, which Socket names, on: every version of every OpenSSF malware entry, not withdrawn, that
#     names the "self-propagating npm supply-chain worm of 2026-08-04" (OSV's npm export of 25 October
#     2026): 2249 versions of 432 packages, less the 25 of @servicetitan/suppress-warnings skipped below,
#     so 2224. GitHub's malware advisories name the same versions for 370 of them and have none for 5;
#     for 56, OpenSSF's entry adds one to five versions GitHub's leaves out; and for the 432nd,
#     @servicetitan/suppress-warnings, GitHub's advisory names all 342 of its versions (skipped below).
#   SANDWORM_MODE, February 2026: the 19 malicious packages of Socket's list (sandworm) and the
#     four it lists as sleeper packages, not malicious yet (sandsleep): GitHub's malware advisories of
#     the same day name every version of each (GHSA-9w7p-hqx2-pjjx, GHSA-m47j-9qfx-6jh4,
#     GHSA-56j5-62q9-cj2c, GHSA-w9hv-7gxr-9f8f) and say a machine that installed one is compromised,
#     and those govern. All but yarsg's: its advisory, GHSA-xw78-h8vv-phcj, also spans a 1000.0.0 that
#     npm's registry dates 2019-04-04, so it is listed at the 18.0.0 and 18.0.1 of 17 February 2026
#   GlassWorm's invisible-code wave, March 2026 (glasswormuni): the two npm packages Aikido's post on it
#     names, at the versions GitHub's malware advisories name: @aifabrix/miso-client 4.7.2
#     No other malware entry names that wave. Its VS Code extension is in data/bad-extensions.tsv.
# npm's registry dates every listed version of the AntV, Red Hat and Mini Shai-Hulud waves to its wave's
# days (19 May, 1 June, and 29 and 30 April 2026), except @cap-js/openapi 1.4.1 (above). A version it
# dates before a wave is not listed and has a skip line below.
# Not listed: every version of four names. tensorlake's advisory also lists every version, but names
# only 0.5.144 as malicious. GitHub's advisory for @tallyui/components spans every version, and
# OpenSSF's entry carries that range too, but the versions it lists, like Wiz's list, are only 1.0.1
# to 1.0.3. GitHub's advisory for @antv/a8 spans every version, and OpenSSF's entry carries that range
# too, but the versions it lists are only 0.1.1 and 0.2.1, and npm's registry keeps only 0.0.1, from
# December 2023. GitHub's advisory and OpenSSF's entry for yarsg span every version, but npm's registry
# dates its 1000.0.0 to 2019-04-04, before the worm.
#! skip tensorlake * the advisory also lists every version, but names only 0.5.144 as malicious
#! skip tensorlake-native-darwin-arm64 0.5.144 Tensorlake's own advisory, GHSA-8g63-53c9-65j2, names it as compromised; no malware entry does
#! skip tensorlake-native-linux-arm64-gnu 0.5.144 Tensorlake's own advisory, GHSA-8g63-53c9-65j2, names it as compromised; no malware entry does
#! skip tensorlake-native-linux-arm64-musl 0.5.144 Tensorlake's own advisory, GHSA-8g63-53c9-65j2, names it as compromised; no malware entry does
#! skip tensorlake-native-linux-x64-gnu 0.5.144 Tensorlake's own advisory, GHSA-8g63-53c9-65j2, names it as compromised; no malware entry does
#! skip tensorlake-native-linux-x64-musl 0.5.144 Tensorlake's own advisory, GHSA-8g63-53c9-65j2, names it as compromised; no malware entry does
#! skip tensorlake-native-win32-x64 0.5.144 Tensorlake's own advisory, GHSA-8g63-53c9-65j2, names it as compromised; no malware entry does

#! skip @tallyui/components * GitHub's advisory spans every version, and OpenSSF's entry carries that range, but the versions OpenSSF's entry lists and Wiz's list names are only 1.0.1 to 1.0.3, published on the day of the wave; 2.0.0 and later came months after

#! skip @antv/a8 * GitHub's advisory spans every version, and OpenSSF's entry carries that range, but the versions it lists are only 0.1.1 and 0.2.1, published in the wave; npm's registry keeps only 0.0.1, from December 2023
#! skip @antv/li-sam-assets 0.1.4 npm's registry dates it 2023-07-10, before the wave; of the sources only GitHub's advisory names it, and its package.json has no install hook
#! skip yarsg * GitHub's advisory and OpenSSF's entry span every version, but npm's registry dates 1000.0.0 to 2019-04-04, before the worm; 18.0.0 and 18.0.1 came out on 17 February 2026
